drafted.title: Unvalidated tool-call and task parameters causing injection, traversal, or crash
drafted.description: An agent, MCP server, or pipeline component accepts tool-call arguments, flow/node definitions, file uploads, or other externally-controlled fields without validating type, range, format, or allowed values before using them in command construction, file paths, deserialization, or model inference, letting an attacker smuggle in malicious payloads. Depending on the sink this yields remote code execution, path traversal, authorization/allowlist bypass, or a crash/denial of service, and because the input often originates from a prompt, a tool response, or another agent, the trust boundary is far less obvious than in a traditional web form.

drafted.title: Unrestricted XML external entity resolution in document-parsing tools
drafted.description: An agent tool or dependency that parses XML-based input (uploaded documents, SAML/SBOM/SVG/config payloads, tool responses fetched from the web) leaves DTD processing and external entity resolution enabled, so an attacker-crafted document containing an external entity reference causes the parser to read local files, issue SSRF requests to internal services, or trigger entity-expansion denial of service. Because the agent treats the parsed content as routine tool input/output, the malicious entity executes silently inside the agent's trust and network context, exfiltrating secrets or pivoting to internal infrastructure.

drafted.title: Downstream command/query execution via unneutralized LLM-generated input
drafted.description: An agent forwards LLM-generated or externally-sourced content (filenames, translated strings, tool arguments, retrieved documents, generated queries/code) directly into a downstream interpreter — a shell, database/graph query engine, template renderer, or markup processor — without neutralizing special characters or syntax tokens. Because the agent trusts its own generated or retrieved text as safe, an attacker who controls any upstream input (a crafted file, document, RAG chunk, or prompt) can smuggle shell metacharacters, Cypher/SQL fragments, or template directives through the pipeline to achieve command execution, query manipulation, or context/role-boundary forgery in the downstream component.

drafted.title: Open redirect via unvalidated redirect/callback URL parameter
drafted.description: An agent-adjacent web component (login flow, OAuth callback, logout route, or MCP registry/client redirect handler) forwards a user- or attacker-supplied URL parameter into an HTTP redirect without validating that it points to an allow-listed origin, letting an attacker craft a trusted-looking link that ultimately redirects the victim (or the agent's browser/tool session) to an attacker-controlled host. This is commonly chained with OAuth/SSO token leakage, credential phishing, or exfiltration of agent session artifacts once the redirect lands on a malicious endpoint.

drafted.title: Unauthenticated cross-origin tool invocation via missing Origin/Host header validation
drafted.description: An MCP server's HTTP/SSE transport accepts requests without validating the Origin or Host header, so a malicious web page rendered in a victim's browser (or an attacker using DNS rebinding against a loopback-bound server) can issue cross-origin requests that the server treats as trusted, invoking arbitrary agent tools and reading their responses without any authentication. Because many MCP servers bind to localhost assuming same-machine trust, this turns an ordinary browser tab into a remote, unauthenticated control channel over the agent's tools and connected systems.

drafted.title: Path traversal via unsanitized filename parameters in agent tool file operations
drafted.description: An agent-facing tool, plugin, or MCP server endpoint accepts a filename/path argument for file upload, save/load, delete, or asset-retrieval operations and concatenates it into a filesystem path without canonicalizing or restricting it to an intended base directory, so an attacker embeds '../' sequences, absolute paths, or symlink tricks to read, overwrite, or write files anywhere the process can access. Because these file-handling tools are routinely exposed to LLM-driven or user-supplied tool calls, this yields arbitrary file read/write (and often code execution via written configs, plugins, or packages) without any model-level jailbreak needed.

drafted.title: Unrestricted file upload via agent tool enabling remote code execution
drafted.description: An agent-exposed upload/ingestion capability (chatbot file attach, 'send file to AI', media/document upload, model-artifact import) fails to validate file extension, MIME type, or content against an allowlist, letting an attacker plant a script, webshell, or executable config in a web-servable or auto-loaded location. The agent's own backend or runtime subsequently executes or interprets that file, giving the attacker full remote code execution on the host rather than just a malicious data artifact.

drafted.title: Arbitrary code execution via eval injection in tool-call and workflow expression parsing
drafted.description: Agent frameworks, orchestrators, and workflow/no-code builders often feed attacker-influenced strings — tool-call arguments, custom-component code, workflow expressions, or even the LLM's own generated output — directly into a language-level eval()/exec()-style evaluator without sandboxing or neutralizing control characters. Because the evaluator runs with the hosting process's full privileges, anyone who can shape that input (a user, a malicious MCP server response, or a manipulated model completion) achieves arbitrary code execution, collapsing the boundary between data the agent reasons over and code it actually runs.

drafted.title: Prototype pollution in dependency library enabling agent runtime RCE
drafted.description: An attacker submits crafted keys such as `__proto__`, `constructor.prototype`, or deep dotted paths through tool input, form data, or workflow configuration that a vulnerable merge/clone/template/parsing function in an agent framework or its JS dependency (e.g. a glob matcher, HTTP client, form parser, or templating engine) writes without sanitizing against prototype traversal. Because the mutated `Object.prototype` is shared process-wide, the attacker can later trigger downstream code paths — validation checks, HTTP request construction, template rendering, or workflow node execution — that read the polluted properties as trusted defaults, turning the pollution into an authorization bypass, response/request tampering, or full arbitrary code execution gadget chain.

drafted.title: Path traversal in agent file-handling endpoints leading to arbitrary read/write
drafted.description: Agent/MCP-adjacent tool and server endpoints (model download, extension install, log viewer, backup/restore, media upload) accept a filename or path parameter and pass it to filesystem APIs without normalizing or constraining it, so attacker-supplied sequences like '../' or absolute/archive-embedded paths escape the intended directory. This lets an unauthenticated or low-privileged caller read sensitive files, overwrite application files, or drop executable payloads (e.g., via tar-slip extraction) that the agent runtime later loads or executes, yielding information disclosure or remote code execution.
